cells.verb: keeping what the change left you
cells.place: in the ongoing work of adjusting
cells.ask: Offer one piece of what you've been keeping to someone, and take what comes back. Settled enough to trade, and the trade only steadies it further.
cells.core:
You're keeping what the change gave you, and you're still adjusting around it. The ground hasn't gone rigid and it hasn't washed out — you add a little, take a little away, and the thing you won stays where you put it. That's not resting on it. That's tending it.

It's steady enough now that it doesn't have to be kept alone. If you want, let one person into the exchange: give some of what you've held and let what they hand back count. Fair trade doesn't have to be measured when the footing is this good — it just moves, and the keeping gets lighter for it.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding what you won while still tuning it — and it's steady enough to share.

cells.tense: Future — bracing for a loss that hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: guarding what the change left you
cells.place: in the ongoing work of adjusting
cells.ask: Let yourself be drawn to one thing you haven't secured yet — a feeling, a person, a possibility — and stay with the pull without closing your hand on it. The grip eases, the endings stop looking like threats, and what's new gets room to come in.
cells.core:
You're guarding what you won against a day it gets taken. Nothing's reaching for it yet, but you're already braced, so the adjusting has stopped being adjusting — every move is a move to lock down. What was meant to stay steady is getting gripped, and gripped things can't be tuned.

The way out isn't to hold tighter or let go. It's to let something you haven't felt yet have a pull on you — one new thing you're drawn to, met as itself, not folded into the pile of what has to be kept. Wanting something unsecured is the opposite muscle from guarding, and using it loosens the hand.
cells.sheetLine: You're clenching what you won against a loss that hasn't come.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at the door of a change that already happened.
cells.verb: letting what the change left you slip through
cells.place: in the ongoing work of adjusting
cells.ask: Pick one direction the change actually pointed you toward and move on it this week, and defend that move when something pushes back. The settling you can't make happen directly follows the moving. What was won gets a place to land, and the ending behind you finally reads as finished.
cells.core:
The change happened and you haven't kept anything from it. You're still adjusting — a little this way, a little that — but nothing gets to settle, so nothing stays. It's all still provisional, as if the ending might be reopened, and you're standing where it closed instead of in what it made.

Trying to feel settled won't fill this. What does is motion toward something you actually want: choose a direction the change pointed at, go, and hold the line when it meets resistance. Having something to stand for gives the harvest a place to be kept.
cells.sheetLine: You went through the change and haven't kept what it gave you.

cells.tense: Present, disowned — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: keeping what the change left you
cells.place: in the ongoing work of adjusting
cells.ask: Name, plainly and once, the thing you've been keeping steady and say that you're the one keeping it. The keeping stops needing luck to explain it, and things make sense around you because you say so.
cells.core:
You're already the steady point. Something the change produced has been held in place for a while, and people lean on it, and you keep adjusting around it without being asked. But you talk about it as if it just happened to hold — the circumstances, the luck, the way things fell.

The holding is yours. It has a shape and a keeper, and the keeper has been declining the credit. There's a simpler way to stand in it: say what's being kept and say that you're keeping it. Clear ownership of what's already true needs no force behind it — it's just the plainest version of what you've been doing anyway.
cells.sheetLine: You've been the one keeping it steady. You've been calling it circumstance.
